title: Emergence of Scale-Free Networks in Social Interactions among Large Language Models
claim_use: Strongest fresh L4 bridge case; can support the statement that L4 exists in widened digital-network bridge evidence, not strict anchor_core.
source_basis: arXiv/ar5iv full text states agents in a growing online-social-network simulation receive a list of all existing users plus each user's number of friends/degree, then choose connections; authors analyze resulting scale-free and hub-and-spoke network structures.
coding_note: Counts as L4 because degree/global network-position information is agent-facing. It is digital-network structure, not physical or virtual spatial configuration.
next_action: Add as a new bridge_core L4 row after duplicate check.

title: Simulating Opinion Dynamics with Networks of LLM-based Agents
claim_use: Useful as LLM opinion-dynamics bridge evidence, but not an L4 recovery case.
source_basis: ACL full text describes pairwise interactions among LLM agents, opinion trajectories, confirmation-bias manipulations, and sensitivity analyses; it explicitly notes that agents interact with everyone and more realistic network structures are future work.
coding_note: Despite the title, the current setup is effectively dyadic/all-to-all interaction rather than agent-facing global topology. Do not code as L4.
next_action: Keep as optional bridge_core L3 if more network/opinion-dynamics coverage is desired; not needed for L4 count.

title: LLM-AIDSim: LLM-Enhanced Agent-Based Influence Diffusion Simulation in Social Networks
claim_use: Useful network-diffusion bridge case; strengthens digital-network L3 but not L4.
source_basis: MDPI full text defines a directed social network, in-neighbours/out-neighbours, LLM user agents, influence diffusion, and updates based on active in-neighbour responses. It supports synthetic or real-world social networks.
coding_note: Agents observe incoming messages and active in-neighbour responses. The paper does not show agent-facing centrality/community/global graph summaries, so L3 not L4.
next_action: Add as bridge_core L3 only if expanding digital-network bridge rows beyond current map.

title: Understanding Online Polarization Through Human-Agent Interaction in a Synthetic LLM-Based Social Network
claim_use: Good observed human-agent online-social-network bridge case; not an L4 recovery case unless full source later shows agent-facing global metrics.
source_basis: arXiv abstract reports a controlled synthetic LLM-based social network with 122 human participants, manipulated polarized environments, and effects on emotionality, group identity salience, and expressed uncertainty.
coding_note: Network environment is central and experimentally manipulated, but current accessible evidence does not show agents receiving global centrality/community/topology summaries. Code as L3 until full text proves otherwise.
next_action: Add as bridge_core L3 observed_effect if human-agent social-network bridge layer is expanded.

title: GoAgent: Group-of-Agents Communication Topology Generation for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
claim_use: Useful for feasibility of communication-topology design in LLM-MAS, not Core spatial-social evidence.
source_basis: arXiv/HuggingFace abstract says GoAgent generates communication topologies for LLM-based MAS by selecting and connecting collaborative groups, improving benchmark accuracy and reducing token cost.
coding_note: This is agent-communication topology for task coordination, not a spatial or socially situated environment. It can support L4 feasibility but should not enter Core evidence map.
next_action: Keep in Adjacent/feasibility notes, not widened Core.
